item.title: Chinese business community urges U.S. to withdraw proposed tariffs
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
BEIJING, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese business community has urged the United States to withdraw its proposed additional tariffs on China and 13 other economies following a Section 301 investigation into alleged "structural excess capacity" in manufacturing sectors, the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT) said Friday.
The Office of the United States Trade Representative recently announced findings of its Section 301 investigation and proposed imposing additional tariffs on 14 economies, including China.
"The Chinese business community firmly opposes this," a CCPIT spokesperson said, adding that the community rejects the claim of "structural excess capacity" as a false narrative and opposes the U.S. side using the allegation as a pretext to interfere in normal China-U.S. economic and trade exchanges.
Assessments of industrial supply and demand conditions should take into account factors including global market demand, technological progress and investment cycles, the spokesperson said. Trade surpluses are shaped by multiple factors such as the international division of labor, market demand and macroeconomic conditions, and trade surpluses alone are insufficient to determine structural excess capacity.
Tariff wars and trade wars benefit no one, the spokesperson said, adding that broad-based tariff hikes will push up procurement costs for U.S. downstream enterprises, place additional burdens on consumers and disrupt global industrial and supply chains.
The Chinese business community calls on the United States to withdraw the proposed tariff measures and resolve relevant issues through consultations with China on the basis of equality, respect and mutual benefit, to maintain stable and sound China-U.S. economic and trade relations, the spokesperson said.
The CCPIT will continue to follow the concerns of Chinese and U.S. enterprises and foster practical cooperation and communication among the business communities of China, the United States and other countries, the spokesperson added.

item.title: Chinese premier chairs State Council executive meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
BEIJING, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Friday chaired a State Council executive meeting, which heard a report on the comprehensive inspection of efforts to promote high-quality development and studied work on further deepening comprehensive investment and financing reforms in the capital market.
The meeting also heard a report on the development of the national standards system, and reviewed and approved a draft regulation on the investigation and rectification of potential workplace safety hazards.
Solid efforts should be made to rectify problems discovered in the inspection, the meeting said, urging action to ensure that all goals and tasks for the year are accomplished to a high standard.
It is imperative to adjust and improve policies and measures that no longer meet the requirements of high-quality development, optimize the incentive and constraint mechanisms, and ensure better coordination of policies, the meeting said.
Stressing that the capital market is vital to overall economic development, the meeting called for efforts to strengthen counter-cyclical adjustments and tackle critical reform tasks at the same time.
The meeting stressed the need to improve market-stabilizing mechanisms, give full play to existing policies, and mull and introduce new measures to promote steady and sound development of the capital market.
According to the meeting, efforts should be made to encourage listed companies to pay more dividends and step up share repurchases, give greater play to state-backed funds in steadying the market, and optimize the quasi-"stabilization fund" function of the state-owned Central Huijin Investment Ltd. to provide sufficient liquidity.
The meeting also underlined the need to improve policies to support and guide medium- and long-term funds such as insurance funds, enterprise annuities, and social security funds into the market, and strengthen the capacity to guard against and respond to imported risks.
It also underlined efforts to boost the internal momentum for high-quality development of the capital market by deepening reform, and to move faster to develop a multi-tiered capital market.
It is imperative to strengthen law-based whole-chain supervision and regulation of the capital market, take firm action against financial fraud, non-compliant share reductions and other violations, and effectively protect the lawful rights and interests of investors.
The meeting also stressed efforts to systematically improve the standards system, with measures including abolishing local standards that do not meet the requirements of building a unified national market, strengthening the supply of high-quality standards, and taking a forward-looking approach to planning standards for emerging industries and future industries.
In terms of workplace safety, the meeting stressed that efforts should focus on key industries and sectors, and that firm measures should be taken to prevent serious and major accidents.

item.title: PLA Army to display Z-20T, other advanced weaponry at Zhuhai airshow
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
A Z-20 helicopter takes part in a flying display at the 14th China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition in Zhuhai, south China's Guangdong Province, on Nov. 8, 2022. (Xinhua/Zhang Yongjin)
BEIJING, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- The Army of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) will stage flight demonstrations with three types of helicopters, the Z-10, Z-20 and Z-20T, at the 16th China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition, also known as Airshow China, the service said Friday.
The airshow is scheduled to take place from Dec. 7 to 13 in Zhuhai, a coastal city in south China's Guangdong Province.
It also marks the Airshow China debut of the Z-20T, the Army said, noting that helicopters carrying assault troops will conduct coordinated operations with ground equipment during the demonstrations, simulating fire strikes and air assault missions to seize and secure key positions.
In total, the PLA Army will present 24 pieces of active-duty main battle equipment across six categories, including the Type 100 tank, at the airshow.
The displays will also feature a range of unmanned and intelligent systems, highlighting the Army's advances in mobile warfare, multidimensional offensive and defensive operations, and the development of unmanned and intelligent capabilities.
Army aviators and special forces personnel will interact with visitors, the service added.
The PLA Air Force and PLA Navy will also showcase advanced weaponry at the airshow, including the J-35A and J-20A stealth fighters, J-16 multirole fighter, Y-20B large transport aircraft, as well as Type 055 destroyer and Type 075 amphibious assault ship.
This year marks the 30th anniversary of Airshow China. Since its inception in 1996, it has become an important platform for showcasing advanced aviation technologies and equipment from China and abroad.

item.title: China launches new remote sensing satellite
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
A modified Long March-6 carrier rocket carrying the Yaogan-50 04 satellite blasts off from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center in north China's Shanxi Province, Nov. 27, 2026. China launched a remote sensing satellite from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center in north China's Shanxi Province on Friday. The Yaogan-50 04 satellite was launched at 9:05 p.m. (Beijing Time) aboard a modified Long March-6 carrier rocket and entered its planned orbit. The launch mission was a complete success. (Photo by Wang Yapeng/Xinhua)
TAIYUAN, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- China launched a remote sensing satellite from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center in north China's Shanxi Province on Friday.
The satellite will primarily be used for land survey, crop yield estimation, and disaster prevention and relief.
The launch marked the 682nd flight mission of the Long March carrier rocket series.

item.title: New growth drivers lift China's industrial profits 16% in first 10 months of 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
Profits of China's industrial firms above designated size rose 16.0% year-on-year to 6.74 trillion yuan ($1 trillion) in the first ten months of 2026, maintaining double-digit growth since the start of the year, data from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) showed on Friday.
The growth rate accelerated by 0.5 percentage points from the January-September period, as emerging growth drivers continued to gain momentum. In October alone, industrial profits climbed 20.1% year-on-year, up 5.7 percentage points from September.
By sector, profits in mining rose 38.8% and manufacturing increased 17.5% in the first 10 months, while those in the production and supply of electricity, heat, gas and water fell 14.8%.
Workers grind and weld inside a pressure vessel production workshop in Rongcheng, Shandong Province, China, November 18, 2026. /VCG
The electronics sector was a major driver of profit growth, with earnings doubling year-on-year during the January-October period. Rising demand for AI computing power continued to boost profits in memory chips and related manufacturing industries, contributing 9.7 percentage points to the growth in total industrial profits, said Yu Weining, chief statistician of the NBS.
High-tech manufacturing also continued to outperform the broader industrial sector, with profits rising 50.9% year-on-year, 34.9 percentage points faster than the overall industrial growth rate, Yu said.
The expansion of large-scale intelligent computing centers drove profits in optical fiber and optical cable manufacturing up 6.7 times and 1.5 times, respectively. Meanwhile, continued development of the aerospace industry lifted profits in spacecraft and launch vehicle manufacturing by 63.2%, while those in aerospace-related equipment manufacturing rose 41.7%.

item.title: Chinese premier to hold '1+10' dialogue with heads of major international economic organizations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
Chinese Premier Li Qiang will hold the "1+10" Dialogue in the city of Xiamen, east China's Fujian Province, on the morning of December 2, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Friday.
According to the spokesperson, Li will hold the dialogue with President of the New Development Bank Dilma Rousseff, President of the World Bank Ajay Banga, Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund Kristalina Georgieva, Director-General of the World Trade Organization Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, Acting Secretary-General of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development Pedro Manuel Moreno, Assistant Director-General of the International Labour Organization Laura Thompson, Secretary-General of the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development Mathias Cormann, General Manager of the Bank for International Settlements Pablo Hernandez de Cos, Chair of the Financial Stability Board Andrew Bailey, and President of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank Zou Jiayi.
The spokesperson said that the theme of the dialogue is "Driving Sustained Growth Through Innovation, Promoting Common Development Through Openness."

item.title: China unveils 2026-2030 services trade development plan, vows further opening up
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
Visitors browse the China Service Case Showcase at the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) at Shougang Park in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Ju Huanzong)
BEIJING, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- China will expand the opening up of its trade in services during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), according to a sector plan released on Thursday.
The plan, jointly issued by eight departments including the Ministry of Commerce, says China will refine the negative list management system for cross-border trade in services, expand market access in an orderly manner, and improve the standardization level of this sector.
The plan also aims to ensure the efficient, convenient and secure cross-border flow of factors including data, personnel, capital and technology. In particular, China will develop service infrastructure for cross-border data flows, deepen international data cooperation, and foster a more digital-friendly environment for trade in services, to facilitate the cross-border flow of data.
"China's opening up in the services sector provides vital certainty to global trade in services," said Yang Zhengwei, vice president of the Development Research Center of the State Council.
This opening up is expected to drive the growth of services trade, and the plan sets corresponding targets. By 2030, China's trade in services should achieve a better balance between imports and exports, according to the plan.
In the first three quarters of 2026, China's imports and exports of services reached 5,768.77 billion yuan (about 859.78 billion U.S. dollars), up 8.5 percent year on year, while the deficit in this sector came in at 1,225.97 billion yuan.
To boost services exports, the plan encourages professional service providers in consulting, accounting, legal, intellectual property and other fields to enhance their international service capabilities. It will also launch dedicated initiatives to promote exports in producer services, tourism services and cultural industries.
Meanwhile, China will expand imports of producer services such as R&D and design, resource recycling and environmental governance. It will also encourage imports of more high-quality consumer services, including healthcare, cultural performances and sporting events. In addition, outstanding foreign audiovisual programs and films will be introduced to Chinese audiences, the plan notes.
Li Bin, deputy head of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, said China's services imports reached more than 620 billion U.S. dollars in 2025, covering travel, intellectual property, transport and business services, making China the world's second-largest importer of services.

item.title: Premier Li: China ready to strengthen cooperation with ADB on regional development
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
Chinese Premier Li Qiang meets with Asian Development Bank (ADB) President Masato Kanda at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, the capital of China, November 26, 2026. /Xinhua
China stands ready to work with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to strengthen cooperation in areas such as regional integration, connectivity and emerging industries, and jointly promote regional development and prosperity, Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Thursday.
Li made the remarks during his meeting with ADB President Masato Kanda in Beijing.
Noting that growing instability and uncertainty in the international situation in recent years have taken a toll on the Asian economy, Li said all parties need to further strengthen regional cooperation.
Chinese President Xi Jinping has called for building an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development, at last week's APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, Li said, adding that China stands ready to work closely with all parties in the region to turn this inspiring vision into reality.
The ADB has long been an important promoter of regional economic integration, and China will continue to support the bank's relevant work, further elevate bilateral cooperation and jointly promote regional development and prosperity, Li said.
Against complex changes in the external environment this year, China's economy has stood firm under pressure and maintained steady progress, injecting much-needed stability and certainty into the Asian and global economies, Li noted.
China will continue to promote high-quality development, accelerate the unleashing of demand in its supersized market, deepen the integration of technological and industrial innovation, and maintain the strong momentum of high-quality, innovation-driven growth, thereby contributing to regional development, he said.
China stands ready to work with the ADB to implement the new country partnership strategy, strengthen cooperation in areas such as regional integration, connectivity and emerging industries, improve the quality and efficiency of bilateral cooperation, and better achieve mutually beneficial and win-win outcomes, Li said.
Kanda congratulated China on its economic resilience and sustained growth amid global economic uncertainties, as well as its remarkable progress in fostering new growth drivers.
Noting that this year marks the 40th anniversary of cooperation between the ADB and China, Kanda said the two sides have made substantial progress in cooperation over the past four decades across a wide range of areas, including infrastructure development, poverty reduction, environmental protection and climate action, and have established a platform for South-South cooperation.
The ADB stands ready to work with China to effectively implement the new country partnership strategy, support Chinese modernization and the implementation of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), and elevate the partnership between the ADB and China to a higher level, Kanda said.
